residual_risks: GitHub validate, CodeQL, passive latest-head Codex review, merge, and post-merge monitoring remain required downstream lifecycle gates.

The v1.0 provider_metadata object remains extension-open for historical compatibility, so semantic_role becomes schema-enforced only in the planned version 2.0 contract; current Go writers emit only model_provider.
Factory PR 267's recorded upstream review-signal process escape is not treated as factoryd qualification or as Lumyn M0 PR-lifecycle proof.
The factoryd bundle and runtime remain unqualified for Lumyn v3.1, and dispatch must stay paused.

state_impact: M0 changes only local CLI result classification, result terminology, executable schema descriptions, fixtures, tests, and documentation; it creates no consumer, provider, credential, network, GitHub, or hosted runtime state.
Recognized unimplemented commands now terminate with one typed command_not_implemented result and exit code 2 instead of creating false-green success state.
source_of_truth_changes: commandImplementationStatus in cmd/lumyn/main.go is the authoritative implemented, unimplemented, or unknown command classifier for the retained command surface.
ADR-0006 is the terminology and migration authority while the five executable v1.0 schemas retain their pre-M0 accepted language exactly.
feedback_plan: Keep process-level CLI envelope tests, schema compatibility fixtures, exit-code tests, coverage, repo-pack validation, GitHub validate, CodeQL, passive latest-head Codex review, and post-merge main monitoring in the promotion loop.
When version 2.0 is introduced, add frozen v1.0 validators, version-discriminated readers, mixed-role negative fixtures, and provenance-preserving migration tests before changing writer defaults.
blast_radius: Scripts that previously treated record, verify, trace, demo, share, or eval as successful placeholders now receive exit code 2 and a typed error, which is the intended BASE-005 correction.
New command-result output adds a model_provider discriminator under the extension-open legacy key, while previously valid v1.0 artifacts continue to validate unchanged.
rollback_or_deletion_test: The change has no external state to delete; a rollback must revert command classification, Go terminology, fixtures, tests, docs, and changelog together and then rerun make prepush-full.
Removing the new discriminator from current writers or narrowing the v1.0 validators must fail the writer and compatibility tests before promotion.
systems_questions.system_model_summary: M0 establishes one fail-closed command-classification boundary and explicit internal Model Provider terminology while preserving the exact v1.0 schema acceptance language; independent local verification and later PR lifecycle gates remain separate authorities.
